theme: Fish runs as birth-star names: Brahmi calibration, discovery exploration and frozen predictions for fresh seals
question: Do the fish compounds on Indus seals form the closed, nearly evenly used class of about 27-28 names that birth-asterism naming would produce, measured against the asterism names of a known naming system in Lüders's 1912 list of Brahmi inscriptions?
outcome: Calibration: of 757 personal donor occurrences in Lüders's list, 42 (5.5%) carry strictly marked asterism names and 57 (7.5%) under the broad marking; they use 12 or 16 of 25 asterism labels, Puṣya supplies 19, and their normalised entropy (0.775, 0.835) is below that of matched non-asterism name elements (median 0.993), which are open (Chao1 2,282). Two independent markings agree with kappa 0.97. Discovery half of seed 2026-10-21-birth-star-names (666 seal legends): the direction note's N1 and N3 fail as written (prefix-plus-run compounds have 60 types and Chao1 186; no modifier distinguishes three bases); N2 is retired because the calibrated birth-star class itself is less even than matched open vocabulary. Fish runs without their stroke prefix have 33 types and Chao1 38.6, match the broad Brahmi profile at 57 occurrences, keep their four commonest forms at 62-75% across Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Lothal and Dholavira, and are independent of the following sign (p = 0.36); runs of other sign families are as closed, and 35.6% of legends carry a fish run against 5.5-7.5% asterism names among Brahmi donors. Five predictions, the scorer and the reference data were frozen through bench shots at 2026-10-21T03:36Z for fresh seals only; C-0013 stands at 0.03. The confirmation half was not read.
challenge: The fish signs have been examined repeatedly, so only seals absent from the pinned corpus can confirm. Two OCR scans with different errors had to be aligned clause by clause; the personal-name index could not be used. The Brahmi asterism class is small (42 or 57 names), so it cannot be bootstrapped to larger samples. Closure and the Brahmi profile do not separate birth-star names from an ordinary closed sign family with the same profile.
remedy: Hashed the protocol and marking rule before extraction; used two independent markers and a logged resolution; kept every marker-A version; froze through the shared loader with nine artifacts and a single joint credence rule in which a closure failure kills the claim and a pass weighs little; replaced an upward bootstrap that rejected the claim's own model with a matched-size comparison and kept the superseded power run; wrote scoring instructions and a scorer that refuses objects already in the pinned corpus and waits for 40 fresh fish runs.
retry_when: Score with the frozen score_fresh.py once at least 40 fish runs in name position are transcribed from seals absent from the pinned corpus (CISI 3.1 or 3.2 absent numbers, Q-1026 finds). A new Indus seed adds no population. A test that can separate birth-star names from an ordinary closed sign family needs observations tied to birth, such as legends naming holder and parent.
